# The Interview Room

---

The fluorescent light above the table buzzed like a dying wasp. Detective Maren Cole leaned back in her chair, arms crossed, watching the man across from her.

Marcus Webb. Thirty-four. Accountant. No priors. His hands hadn't stopped moving since they'd brought him in—fingers drumming, rubbing his knuckles, adjusting the wedding ring he wore on his right hand.

"You want some water?" Maren asked.

"No. I'm fine."

His voice cracked on *fine*.

Maren uncrossed her arms and slid a thin manila folder across the table. She didn't open it. "Marcus, we've got the security footage."

His face went white. "What?"

"From the jewelry store. The night of the break-in." She tapped the folder. "It's pretty clear."

"I wasn't—" He stopped. Swallowed. "I don't know what you're talking about."

"Funny. Because the man in the video looks a lot like you."

"That could be anyone."

"Could be." Maren shrugged. "But the timestamp matches the exact window when the safe was cracked. And we pulled partial prints from the scene." She paused, letting that land. "Care to explain why your prints would be on a safe that hasn't been touched in six months?"

Marcus's mouth opened. Closed. His eyes darted to the folder, then to the two-way mirror, then back to Maren.

"I don't—I haven't been in that store. I don't even—" His voice pitched upward. "This is insane. I didn't do anything."

"People usually say that."

"Because it's true!"

Maren tilted her head. "Then explain the prints."

"I *can't* explain them because they shouldn't be there!" He was gripping the edge of the table now, knuckles white. "Unless—maybe I touched something when I was in the store once? For work? I do taxes for them, I think, or—or maybe I went in to pick something up for my wife, I don't—"

"You're spiraling, Marcus."

"I'm not spiraling, I'm—" He pressed both palms flat against the table, breathing hard. "I need a lawyer."

Maren's expression didn't change. "You want to lawyer up? Now?"

"I have the right to—"

"You do. But if you lawyer up now, that tells me you're guilty." She leaned forward. "It tells me you're trying to hide something."

"I'm trying to protect myself! Isn't that what you're supposed to do?"

"From what?"

He stared at her. His jaw worked silently.

Maren waited.

"I didn't steal anything," he finally said, quieter now. "I swear to God. I don't even know what's in that safe. I don't know anything about jewelry."

"Then why are you shaking?"
